headline: Jeff Bezos reportedly eyeing 30% stake in Liverpool FC for $1.8 billion
summary: The Amazon founder, along with Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin, is looking to acquire a significant share in the English soccer team, valued at £1.35 billion. This marks his first reported sports investment.
details: Jeff Bezos is reportedly attempting to join other wealthy Americans in buying stakes in U.K. soccer teams. He, along with Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin, is looking to acquire at least a 30% stake in the English soccer team Liverpool. The deal is valued at £1.35 billion (around $1.8 billion), according to The Guardian.

If the deal closes, this would be Bezos's first sports investment, though he previously considered a U.S. football team. Liverpool is one of Europe's most notable sports teams, with Forbes valuing it at approximately $6 billion. Its brand recognition in the U.K. is comparable to that of the Dallas Cowboys in the U.S.

The trend of billionaires and celebrities owning stakes in English soccer teams has grown, partly fueled by popular TV shows like "Ted Lasso" and "Welcome to Wrexham." Other American billionaires in this club include Todd Boehly (Chelsea) and Woody Johnson (Crystal Palace), among others.

Soccer's increasing popularity in the U.S. makes Premier League teams attractive, as top U.S. franchises like the NFL and MLB are often too expensive or closed off. Sky Sports reported that 13 out of 20 Premier League clubs have American shareholders.

Owning a share in such a team offers access to highly recognizable sports icons. Bezos, with his evolving public image since marrying Lauren Sánchez, is increasingly seen as a cultural figure beyond just a tech mogul.

With a net worth of around $280 billion, Bezos's interest in a sports team is not surprising. Amazon has previously streamed European soccer leagues, and Bezos has growing interests in the U.K., including his AI company Prometheus reportedly seeking a lease in London's AI hub.

summary: Apple has agreed to settle a religious discrimination lawsuit brought by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) last year.
details: Apple has reached a settlement in a religious discrimination lawsuit. The U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) filed the suit last year, alleging discrimination against a Jewish employee.
